newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end mostly up on short covering.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end mostly up on short covering.

text.p: Short covering again supported most months of CME lumber futures, but the nearby again ended lower, pressured by a weak cash market and rolling of longs into back months, traders said.
Lumber closed $1.50 lower to $3.20 per tbf higher with only March off at $383.50 and May up $0.70 at $380.00 per tbf.

Short covering ahead of the weekend kept the market support, especially after the drop in futures to lowest levels in two months, basis March. However, a continued weak tone in the cash market kept a lid on futures. Cash trade remained very slow, they said.
Random Lengths on Friday quoted cash spruce for the week down $14 at $400 per tbf.

Adding to pressure in March at times was rolling of longs in back months ahead of its spot position on Monday. There are no limits in spot month and open interest has been falling as liquidation continues, they said.
The National Association of Realtors reported January existing home sales up 2.1 percent at 3.94 million annual rate. Economists had forecast sales at a 3.89 million unit annual rate.
